correctness.rationale: The nonzero bidegree-(e,d) resultant gives singularity of a Gram matrix indexed by (e+1)(d+1) Hardy vectors. Vanishing at the origin eliminates all comparable-index offdiagonal terms; the remaining row degree is at most de. A singular Hermitian unit-diagonal matrix cannot have all off-diagonal entries bounded by a number strictly smaller than 1/de. Coprime monomials prove exponent-cutoff optimality, and degree-one equality verifies the boundary. These steps are complete for all positive degrees.
